design_system_intro: What hexframe holds is a perspective, one a person crafts over a lifetime and that agents keep working with. The look is futuristic because hexframe is a bet on a future worth wanting: space, imbalance, fine lines and light, not chrome.
design_system_principle_space_text: Nothing is centered for its own sake: the tiles run on behind the conversation instead of stopping at a frame. A screen is never filled to show it is busy.
design_system_principle_light_text: A surface is drawn by its light, not by an outline: a tile is a fill, lighter than the ground. Where a separator is needed, it is a hairline or a curve, never a box.
design_system_principle_root: One warm light, at the root
design_system_principle_root_text: Amber belongs to the human: your own tile holds its one warm light. The center you look at gets a neutral line, since amber says “you”, not “here”.
design_system_principle_voices: A warm human, a cool agent
design_system_principle_voices_text: Your words are set in Newsreader, a light serif; the agent's in Geist Mono, marked in violet. The interface speaks quietly, in Geist, so the two voices carry the page.
design_system_principle_curves_text: The conversation is cut along one curve, which also serves as its scrollbar, and the layout meets the geometry of the tiles.
design_system_principle_motion_text: Moving to a neighbour pans; to a child or a parent zooms; an opened tile's children bloom out of its heart. With reduced motion, everything lands at once.
design_system_screen: Dark is the default and light its equal. hexframe is one screen with two sides: the Chat, where you and the agent act, and the Canvas, which carries what you act on. Below, the crossings between them, each side's pieces, what the sides share, then the tokens.
design_system_tier_crossings_note: Where one side answers the other, both ways: a tile named in the chat lights up on the canvas, a tile centered on the canvas is where the agent works next.
design_system_tier_chat_note: It shows the Conversation: you and the agent act there, and whatever a menu would do happens there.
design_system_tier_canvas_note: It shows the System: what you and the agent act on, and the way through it.
design_system_tier_layouts_note: Shells with slots that both sides share: they decide where things go and how they fold on a phone.
design_system_tier_atoms_note: Controls that both sides share and that know nothing of hexframe.
design_system_tier_seams_note: A library behind one file, which any piece may draw with: that file alone changes when the library comes or goes.
gallery_note_conversation: The chat on home, on fixtures: Assistant's timeline a day at a time, on the chat's pieces, and the composer with the commands home runs. A tile named centers the canvas below.
gallery_note_message: The two voices: your words in Newsreader behind an amber line, dimmed while sending, destructive with a retry once refused; the agent's in Geist Mono behind its violet mark, inking in word by word while they come. Both copy from the edge of the column.
gallery_note_thinking: The agent's thinking, quieter than its words, on a dotted violet line: live, its last lines scroll past; once it has answered, it folds into how long it thought, open on a click.
gallery_note_mention: A tile named, wherever it is: its title, a small hex, a faint underline; a click centers the canvas on it. Hovered or focused, it opens the tile's card, as the tile does on the canvas, and the canvas lights the tile, or the nearest tile on its way when it isn't drawn. Violet while the agent drafts it, struck through once deleted.
gallery_note_events: What happens between the two voices, one line each on a thread of small hexes coloured by who acted: amber for you, violet for the agent, hollow for a Key. A navigation, a change, the live step, a Turn's end; a run of reads folds into one line.
gallery_note_day_split: Where a day begins: its name, faint, then a hairline that fades toward the curve. A line, never a box.
gallery_note_proposal: What the agent proposes in ask: a widget in its voice with its changes, Accept and its ⌘↵, and Discard, asked first. Once decided, it gives its surface back and leaves its receipt, where the focus lands.
gallery_note_receipt: The one line a decision leaves: what was done, its Undo while one is possible, then that it was undone, and its changes, folded until asked for. An accepted Proposal and a Turn that applied its changes leave one alike; a discarded Proposal keeps what it would have changed.
gallery_note_fold: One line that opens what it hides below it, a chevron turning as it does: the thinking once done, a run of reads. Quiet until pointed at.
gallery_note_composer: Where the user writes to the agent. A / at the start lists the commands, which take the place of a menu; an @ anywhere finds a tile by its title, and the canvas lights the one whose row is active; both rise from the composer's top line, and the field keeps the keys. Under it, what the agent may do and where it works next: the tile the message names first, else the one centered; while it works, send becomes Stop. A tile carried from the canvas is named where the user lets it go. On a phone it rides above the keyboard, its rows a thumb's height.
gallery_note_canvas: The System as tiles: a Tile, the six around it, and theirs. Its view lives in the address, so a link shows what its sender saw.
gallery_note_breadcrumb: Where you are on a System: the way from the root to the centered Tile, drawn as the canvas's Rail in its corner, the theme at its head; a step centers the canvas on it.
gallery_note_channels: Where a failure shows, picked by its kind and by the call that met it, never by a component's author. Signed out, any call goes to sign-in; a read that frames every page shows nothing of its failure, which is reported.
gallery_note_confirm_dialog: Asks before a step that is hard to take back: a Proposal discarded, a Tile deleted.
gallery_note_widget: Everything the conversation asks of you or shows you beyond words, in one shape learned once: an icon, a kicker, a title, a body, its actions, and its tools when you reach for them. Tinted by whose it is; working, it breathes; done, it leaves one line, its receipt.
gallery_note_hover_card: What a tile cuts short, in full, beside it, whether the tile is on the canvas or named in the chat: after a moment under the pointer, at once on keyboard focus. Opened from the chat, the card points at the tile, which the canvas lights. A finger can't hover, so under one it never opens: on the canvas, the long press opens the tile's menu, whose header says the same.
gallery_note_dialog: The one thing that stops you, kept for what can't be undone or loses work. Wide, it opens over the conversation's column, so the canvas stays in view and shows what it touches; on a phone, it rises from the bottom as a sheet.
gallery_note_menu: Everything you can do to a thing, where it is, by a right click, a long press or ⇧F10, or behind a control. Each line carries its key, which runs it, so the menu teaches the keys. Under a finger, its header says what the hover card would.
gallery_note_act: An action as a word led by a small hex, the one a widget expects in its voice with its shortcut; or the one solid act a dialog asks for, a light cut as a long hex.
gallery_note_empty_state: What a place shows while it holds nothing, and the action that fills it.
gallery_note_error_state: What a read's boundary shows when the read failed: what happened, the request's id to quote, and a retry.
gallery_note_forbidden: What a read's boundary shows when what it holds isn't yours to see.
gallery_note_button: Quiet by default, in the ink: colour is kept for the human and the agent.
gallery_note_textarea: Several lines of text, in the same states as Input.
gallery_note_field: A control with its label, its description and its errors, tied together for a screen reader.
gallery_note_use_app_form: A form with its fields drawn: each shows its error once touched, and a form reopened by a refusal shows it.
gallery_note_toaster: Where a write's failure and a passing word show, then go.
gallery_note_skeleton: The shape of what is loading, in its place.
gallery_note_theme_toggle: Dark or light, kept on the device: a half-lit disc that turns half a turn as the light changes, since a change of theme is a change of light. On the screen it heads the canvas's corner.
gallery_note_code_block: A Body that isn't Markdown, shown as it is written; a long line scrolls.
gallery_state_chat_agent_run: The agent's answer, a run of two: the mark on the first only
gallery_state_chat_thinking_done: Done, folded: open on a click
gallery_state_chat_mention_agent: In the agent's words: a click centers the canvas
gallery_state_chat_operations: Changes, by who made them: you, the agent, a Key, a revoked Key
gallery_state_chat_navigation: A navigation, and how many moves it merged
gallery_state_chat_reads: A run of reads, folded: open on a click
gallery_state_chat_live_step: The agent's step, live, and one that failed
gallery_state_chat_day: A day, as the chat reads it
gallery_state_chat_proposal_waiting: Waiting: accept it, or discard it, asked first
gallery_state_chat_proposal_pending: While a decision is on its way
gallery_state_chat_receipt_undo: A Turn's changes applied, with the Undo
gallery_state_chat_receipt_pending: While the Undo is on its way
gallery_state_composer_command_tile: A command that takes a tile
gallery_state_composer_running: A turn running: send becomes Stop
gallery_state_composer_waiting: Disabled, until the page can send
gallery_state_composer_phone: On a phone, over its keyboard
gallery_composer_sample_writing: Draft the page for @Tooling, from what @Projects says
gallery_canvas_how: Click the folded center to open it, and again to fold it back; click a branch to open or close it in place; double-click a tile, or press Shift+Enter on it, to center it, alone. Its menu, a right click away, shows its context.
gallery_channels_read_failed: A read failed, in its boundary
gallery_channels_read_missing: A read of what no longer exists
gallery_channels_write: A write's failure, in a toast
gallery_channels_submit: A form's refusal, on its field
tokens_intro: What each token is for. They are read from the stylesheet, so none is missed; switch the theme to see the other half.
tokens_colour_ground: The ground and the ink: a violet-black and a near-white at night, a cool paper and a violet-black by day.
tokens_colour_surface: A surface risen a little toward light: a zone of the conversation, a card, a menu.
tokens_colour_primary: The ink itself. A primary button is quiet; colour is kept for the human and the agent.
tokens_colour_step: One step off the ground, for a hovered row, a pressed tab, a field's well. Text in muted-foreground is second-level: a preview, the agent's words.
tokens_colour_faint: Third-level text: a placeholder, a step of the path you are not on, an empty slot's plus.
tokens_colour_hairlines: The hairlines: border between things, input a little stronger, under a field or around the center.
tokens_colour_ring: Keyboard focus, in the human's amber.
tokens_colour_human: The human's amber, for lines and marks: the rule beside your words, the brand mark, the send button, the step of the path you are on.
tokens_colour_agent: The agent's violet: its mark, its words' accents, what it drafts. Dark enough to set text in, by day too.
tokens_colour_statuses: The statuses, each with its foreground. Warning is an ember orange, away from the human's amber.
tokens_colour_context: The Context's teal on the canvas; it only strokes and tints, so it has no foreground.
tokens_colour_glow: The root's warm light, for its fill and its rim.
tokens_colour_halo: The glow behind the root, at its theme's strength: full at night, softer on paper.
tokens_colour_aura: The wide warm haze around the halo.
tokens_colour_ambient: The cool light where the canvas looks.
tokens_colour_dusk: The night side of the brand mark, the same in both themes: the root's glow mixed into it in oklch runs through coral, rose and plum.
tokens_colour_tile: A tile's light, at its top and its foot.
tokens_colour_tile_lit: The same, brighter: the center, and a tile under the pointer.
tokens_colour_chart: The human, the agent, the Context, info, faint.
tokens_colour_sidebar: shadcn's sidebar, on the same surfaces.
tokens_type_sans: Geist, the interface: labels, buttons, previews.
tokens_type_serif: Newsreader: your words, titles and headings, at weight 300 for prose.
tokens_type_mono: Geist Mono: the agent's words, and code.
tokens_type_sizes: The size of your words, 18px, and the agent's, 13.5px. On the canvas a title is laid out at 16px and scaled with its tile, never above 22px nor, on a small tile, below 11px.
tokens_shape: No radius: corners are square, as a hex's are. Round things are round on purpose, not by a token.
tokens_shape_lift: A risen surface's shadow: a menu, a card, the dialog, each drawn with the risen utility, the popover's light and one fine line on top. Deep at night; by day a soft violet shade, so paper still reads as paper.
tokens_motion_glide: Things that settle: a bloom, the theme's disc, the star's glow.
tokens_motion_camera_ease: The camera, easing in and out.
tokens_motion_bloom: Children blooming out of their parent's heart.
tokens_motion_stagger: Between one child and the next.
tokens_motion_camera: A move on the same level, a pan.
tokens_motion_camera_level: Added per level crossed, up to two.
tokens_motion_breathe: A light that waits: the agent working, a draft.
tokens_motion_entrance: A widget coming in: its top line draws itself, the surface unfolds from it, then its parts rise one after another. With reduced motion, it is simply there.
tokens_motion_sweep: Light running over the lines still to come while something works, and over a tile whose write is on its way, never a spinner.
tokens_phone: Two questions. The width picks the layout: below sm, 40rem, is a phone, which shows one side at a time, and the screen reads it on its own width (container-wide); a tablet keeps the wide layout. A finger picks the behaviour, at any width, and needs no token: under a coarse pointer nothing waits on a hover, and a target is at least 44px.
tokens_light_tile: A tile fills with tile fading to tile-fade, top to foot, with no stroke. Under the pointer it brightens to tile-lit.
tokens_light_center: The center fills with tile-lit fading to tile-lit-fade, with an input line, its title in italics.
tokens_light_root: The root fills with glow at 34% fading to glow-soft at 6%. Its rim, when it is the center, runs from glow-soft to human.
tokens_light_halo: The root's glow is a radial halo, its radius growing with the square root of the zoom so it never floods the screen, inside an aura two and a half times wider. Below the root it softens, and waits at the screen's edge once the root is off screen.
tokens_light_ambient: The ambient is a wide ellipse of ambient where the canvas looks.
tokens_light_zone: A zone of the conversation is card, tinted toward its right edge by 9% of the voice it belongs to, with an input hairline on top.
tokens_light_draft: A draft by the agent fills with agent at 14% fading to nothing, behind a blurred agent glow that breathes.
gallery_note_screen: hexframe's one screen, with no menu and no page to go to. Wide, the chat is a column on the left, cut along one curve that is its scrollbar, and the canvas fills the screen behind it, its center off to the right, its tiles running on under the conversation. On a phone one side is in front, the chat first; a tap or a drag on the seam turns it. When the chat points at a tile, the canvas comes forward to show it, then gives the chat back after a glance, the focus where it was, unless a hand took the canvas meanwhile; a screen reader hears what it showed. Signed out it is the same screen: Help on the canvas, and the chat asking who you are.
gallery_note_rail: Where you are, top right of the canvas: one thin line from the root down to the Tile you are on, a point per step, threaded on it with what heads it, the theme's disc on the screen, so the corner reads as one mark rather than a button beside a list. A step up the line centers the canvas on it.
gallery_state_phone: On a phone: a tap or a drag on the seam turns it
gallery_screen_line_1: Show me where design work sits today.
gallery_screen_line_2: Nowhere on its own. The tokens live inside hexframe's app, next to its components, and the site has none yet.
gallery_screen_line_3: I want the design system to live outside hexframe, so my site can use it too.
gallery_screen_line_4: Then it belongs beside Projects rather than inside one. I drafted Design system east of Software Engineering, next to Principles, where principles become something you can reuse.
gallery_screen_line_5: One choice before I write its first page: move hexframe's tokens there now, or when the site needs them?
gallery_screen_line_6: Now. And dark stays the default.
signed_out_help: This is hexframe's help, on the canvas: what a system is, its tiles, and how they hold together. Click its tile to open it; it opens like any system.
signed_out_sign_in: Sign in, and the canvas shows your own.
tokens_container_wide: Where the screen turns wide: Tailwind's sm, read on the screen's own width rather than the window's, so a phone's specimen folds as a phone does. Below it, one side is in front.
gallery_note_tile_widget: A tile written where you talk about it, its title the widget's own: amber while the words are yours, violet while they are the agent's draft. Its hex is the place, the free slots dashed, so a pick moves the tile. Edits mark what changed; a refused write comes back with your words and the refusal on the field. An import and an export happen here too.
gallery_note_key_widget: How an agent outside hexframe reaches your system, in the conversation rather than on a page. The app's own widget, so it carries no voice: a name, the key shown once beside the command that uses it, then the keys you gave, each revoked after a question. Opened by the agent, it shows them and issues none.
gallery_note_help_widget: Help where you are, rather than on another page. Its hex is Help's own frame, the topic lit, and a pick turns the page, so the map is also the way around; the page, then where to read on. /help and a few words list the topics they show in; ? shows the shortcuts.
gallery_note_sign_in_widget: Signed out, the chat asks who you are where you would write: at its foot, on the composer's zone, warm for you. An email and a password on their underlines, the one solid act, and the way between signing in and signing up. A refusal shows on the field at fault.
tokens_motion_ink: A secret inking in from a blur the one time it shows, so the eye knows it is new and rare.

gallery_tile_sample_rest: : the editor, the agents, and the scripts that keep a repository honest.
gallery_tile_sample_body:
## Agents

Claude Code, with the mods this repository ships.

## Checks

The rule of 6, cubic’s three reviewers, dependency-cruiser.
gallery_tile_sample_body_added:
## Shortcuts

The scripts I run before every pull request.
gallery_tile_sample_long: Every tool earns its place by what it saves me, and the ones that stopped saving anything are listed below, with the day I dropped them and why, so I never pick one up again by accident.
tile_kind_reference: a Reference to a tile elsewhere
tile_kind_broken: a Reference whose tile was deleted
tile_kind_list: a ring too full, as a list
tile_untitled_preview: Give it a name, or import a vault.
gallery_note_tile: A tile, drawn by its light alone: what it is, where it stands, what happens to it and who touches it change that light, and never add a box. The canvas draws one per Tile; HEX-106 puts it there in place of today's.
gallery_note_slot: A Direction that holds no tile: a plus only where a click adds one, so the canvas never offers what it can't do; a dotted place where nothing can be added; a sweep of light where tiles will be.
gallery_note_ground: What a hex gives way to when it opens in place: a faint ground under the tile at its heart and its six, or the center's Context, teal and dashed, since it is what the center is rather than what it holds.
gallery_tile_kinds_note: Its light says what it is before its words do: a Branch fades toward its foot, where its frame shows in small; a Leaf is lit evenly; the Context is teal; the root, warm, is you.
gallery_tile_states_note: To your hand, by its place, and over time, each by its light: lit under the pointer, lined at the center, dimmed away from it, blooming out of its parent and folding back. Try the first one with the mouse or the keyboard.
gallery_tile_frame_note: Open a Branch of the ring: its light gives way to a ground, the Branch at its heart and its six blooming out of it; a click on its heart folds them back. A click on the center folds its ring back into it, which leaves it alone and large, its preview whole; another opens it again. The frame scales with the page, and its words fit the size it shows at.
gallery_tile_words_note: A tile's words grow with it, then stop: its title is laid out at 16px and scaled with the tile, never above 22px; under a radius of 72 it shows alone, never below 11px; under a radius of 30, where 11px no longer fits, the tile is a light without words. Its preview, at two thirds of the title, takes as many lines as the hex holds, then an ellipsis.
gallery_tile_root: Your system's own tile, the only warm one, its halo behind.
gallery_tile_branch: Holds tiles: its light fades to its foot, where its frame shows, a dot where each child is.
gallery_tile_bare_branch: Nothing inside yet: its frame, empty.
gallery_tile_leaf: A page, nothing below: its light even, no frame at its foot.
gallery_tile_file: A Leaf that isn't Markdown, by its file's name, in mono.
gallery_tile_context: What its parent is: teal, and one hairline.
gallery_tile_reference: A tile from elsewhere: dashed, and where it lives.
gallery_tile_broken: Its tile was deleted: the place stays, faint, and says so.
gallery_tile_untitled: The root before anything, its rim dashed, waiting for a name or a vault.
gallery_tile_clash: A Leaf numbered as a Branch already is: ember, seated beside it.
gallery_tile_list: More than six to seat: ember, and the names as a list.
gallery_tile_draft: The tile it is writing, in its violet, breathing, its title in mono.
gallery_tile_rest: Its light alone. Hover it, tab to it, press it.
gallery_tile_pointed: Under the pointer, its light rises.
gallery_tile_focused: From the keyboard: the ring's amber line.
gallery_tile_pressed: Lit, and a hair smaller while held.
gallery_tile_center: Lit, the one steady line, its title in italics; its frame is around it, so none at its foot.
gallery_tile_leaf_center: No ring to show: it fills the canvas alone, and takes no click.
gallery_tile_bloom: Out of its parent's heart, 800ms, its siblings 40ms apart. With reduced motion, it is simply there.
gallery_tile_fold: Back into it, 500ms. With reduced motion, simply gone.
gallery_tile_pending: Shown at once as it will be; a moment later, while the server hasn't answered, light sweeps over it. With reduced motion, a still sheen.
gallery_tile_refused: A destructive glow, and it goes back to how it was; why, in a toast or on its form.
gallery_sample_long_title: How we decide together, and where agents could help
gallery_sample_long_title_preview: Politics read as a system: who decides what, and what an agent could carry.
gallery_tile_slot_free: Where a click adds a tile: a plus.
gallery_tile_slot_void: Where nothing can be added, Help or a read-only view: dotted, no plus.
gallery_tile_loading: Light sweeps where tiles will be, no spinner.
tokens_motion_flare: A refusal: a destructive glow rises over the tile and fades.
gallery_state_tile_widget_context: A new Context tile, in Context's colour
gallery_state_tile_widget_draft: The agent's draft: accept it, or edit it, the widget turning yours
gallery_state_tile_widget_refused: Refused and put back: your words, the refusal on the field
tokens_motion_glide_duration: A tile moved, gliding to the slot it lands in, or back to its own once refused.
tokens_motion_ants: The tile on the move: its rim, a dashed line in your amber, running. With reduced motion it holds still.
tile_moving_banner_after: : a free slot, or a Branch to trade places with
gallery_note_tile_menu: Everything you can do to a tile, where it is: a right click, a long press, ⇧F10 or the menu key opens its menu, which names it, then offers what its kind and place allow, grouped by distance, each line with its key, which runs it on the focused tile too. Where the action is a place, adding a tile or moving this one, the submenu is the frame itself. Its hover card says in full what the tile cuts short. HEX-107 puts both on the canvas, in place of the card beside it and the Move mode.
gallery_note_moving: A tile goes where you put it: dragged, or through its menu, whose frame is the keyboard's way and a finger's. While it moves, it lifts, its rim running in your amber; each free slot offers itself and each Branch its swap, at its foot, apart from its own click; the rest steps back; a banner says what moves, and Escape or Stop ends it. It glides to where it lands, the write sent as it lands; refused, it flares, glides back, and the move goes on. A finger never drags a tile: its way is the long press, then the menu. Carried off the canvas under a mouse or a pen, it follows the pointer over the page, for the composer to name it where it is let go.
gallery_tile_menu_live_note: Right-click a tile or a free slot, press and hold it, or focus it and press ⇧F10. Hover a tile, or focus it, for its card. A line's key runs it on the focused tile too: E, M, C… A click, or a tap, says what it would do: under a finger a tap goes into a Branch, since a finger has no double click, and opening it in place waits in its menu. Nothing here changes the System: a toast says what would.
gallery_state_tile_menu_live: Software Engineering and its ring, each tile in its menu and its card
gallery_tile_menu_kinds_note: Each kind's menu, held open. The center backs out and never moves; a Leaf holds no tile, so adds none; a Reference is removed, never deleted with the tile it points at; the agent's draft waits for the agent; a free slot takes a new tile, an import or the agent's.
gallery_tile_menu_finger_note: A tap goes in, the double click a finger lacks. The long press opens the menu, whose header carries what the hover card would, which never opens. Moving waits in the menu, its frame a place to tap; a finger never drags a tile, since a drag pans. Every line and every place is 44px tall at least.
gallery_state_tile_menu_broken: A Reference whose tile is gone
gallery_moving_live_note: Drag a tile with the mouse, or pick one above, as its menu's "Somewhere else…" would; M on a tile opens its menu at its frame (above). Then a free slot, or a Branch's swap at its foot, by a click, by Tab and Enter, or by letting go of the drag over it. Escape or Stop ends it. With the server refusing, the tile flares and glides back, and the move goes on.
gallery_state_moving_live: Software Engineering and its ring, a tile on the move
gallery_moving_frame: A frame where a tile moves
gallery_moving_refused: Refused: the tile went back, and it is still on the move.
gallery_moving_parts_note: What each place becomes while a tile moves.
gallery_moving_lifted: Lifted a little, lit, its rim a dashed line in your amber that runs. Dragged, it follows the pointer.
gallery_moving_landing: Dashed in your amber: any free slot of the frame takes the tile, whatever its kind.
gallery_state_moving_landing_over: Under the pointer, or the drag
gallery_moving_landing_over: It warms and says where the tile would go.
gallery_state_moving_swap: A Branch, offering to trade places
gallery_moving_swap: A small hex with two arrows at its foot, a button apart from the tile's own click, which still opens it.
gallery_moving_aside: The parent, a Leaf, a Reference: a third of its light, and no hover.
tokens_motion_glint: Someone touching a tile: a glow rises over it once and fades, as a refusal's flare does but slower, in their colour, your amber, the agent's violet, a Key's hollow light.
tokens_motion_orbit: The agent working in a tile: its light runs round the rim while the Turn lasts. With reduced motion it holds still.
tokens_motion_glance: On a phone, how long the canvas stays in front once the chat brought it forward to show a tile, before it gives the chat back, unless you take it.
tile_kind_ghost: a tile the agent proposes, not there yet
tile_mark_unseen_agent: changed by the agent, not opened since
tile_mark_unseen_key: changed by a Key, not opened since
gallery_note_marks: Who touches a tile, on its light: you in your amber where the chat points, the agent in its violet as it reads, works, writes and changes, a Key from outside hollow, and what a Proposal would do, dashed violet since it isn't done yet. What changed while you looked away stays as a dot until you open the tile. A screen reader hears what lasts from the tile itself, as its hover card says it.
gallery_marks_yours_note: Where the chat points, and what you write: amber says you, never here.
gallery_marks_agent: The agent, in violet, and a Key, hollow
gallery_marks_agent_note: The agent at work, as its Turn's live step goes, and an agent outside, through a Key.
gallery_marks_proposed_note: Asking first, the agent's changes wait for you: dashed violet is what isn't done yet. Accepted in the chat, they land; discarded, they go.
gallery_mark_pointed: A row of the @ list, or a tile named and hovered: lit, your amber held behind it while the chat points.
gallery_state_mark_way: The way to a tile off the canvas
gallery_mark_way: What the chat points at stands below this tile, off the canvas: the way to it, fainter. A click on the name goes there.
gallery_state_mark_yours: Your change, or where the chat went
gallery_mark_yours: Your amber rises once: a change of yours lands, or the canvas arrives at a tile the chat named. It leaves no dot: you saw it.
gallery_mark_writing: Written in the tile widget: in its slot, breathing in your amber, its words as you type them.
gallery_mark_reads: A violet light passes over it once, as the events list the read.
gallery_mark_working: The tile the Message named first, or the one centered: the agent's light runs round its rim while the Turn lasts.
gallery_mark_drafting: In its slot, in the agent's violet, breathing, its title in its mono.
gallery_mark_changed: Applying with undo: a violet glint, then a dot until you open the tile. Its card says what changed, and when.
gallery_mark_key: An agent outside, Claude Code on a laptop: a hollow glint and a hollow dot. Its card names the Key and when.
gallery_mark_ghost: A ghost in its slot: dashed violet, its title in the agent's mono. It has no menu: the chat decides it.
gallery_mark_edit: The tile as it is, its rim dashed violet; the chat shows the edit where it falls.
gallery_mark_delete: The tile steps back, its rim dashed violet.
gallery_mark_move: Its rim dashed violet, and an arc to the slot it would land in.
gallery_mark_move_label: {center}'s ring: the agent proposes moving {tile} south-west
composer_place_first: the agent works in {title}, named first
composer_drop_here: Let go here to name {title} in your message
crossing_pointing_answer: Start with {near}: {deep} is the one being built, and {beside} says why.
crossing_turn_ask: Give my tools a place under {engineering}, and tighten {principles}'s preview.
crossing_turn_answer: {tooling} holds your tools now, and {principles}'s preview is tighter.
gallery_note_crossing_pointing: A tile pointed at in the chat lights up on the canvas, in your amber: the row of the @ list you are on, or a tile named in a message, hovered or focused, its card open beside it. Off the canvas, the way to it lights, fainter. A click on the name goes there, and the tile glints as the canvas arrives.
gallery_note_crossing_agent: The agent at work, on the canvas as the chat tells its Turn: each tile it reads glints violet once, its light runs round the tile the Turn works in, a tile it writes breathes in its slot, and what it changed glints, then keeps a dot until you open it. An agent outside, through a Key, marks the same way, hollow.
gallery_note_crossing_proposal: Asking first, the agent's Proposal waits in the chat, and on the canvas as ghosts: a tile it would create stands dashed violet in its slot, an edit dashes the tile's rim, a move draws its arc, a deletion steps the tile back. A change pointed at in the Proposal lights its tile. Accepted, they land, glinting in your amber; discarded or undone, they go.
gallery_note_crossing_drafting: A tile being written in the chat's tile widget stands in its slot on the canvas, breathing in the voice of whoever writes it, your amber here, the agent's violet for its draft. Its title follows what is typed; another place picked on the widget's map moves it there. Created, it is there, glinting once.
gallery_note_crossing_next_turn: The tile centered on the canvas is where the next Turn works, and the composer says so under its field. A Message that names a tile first works there instead, which it says too. Sent, the agent's light runs round that tile while the Turn lasts.
gallery_note_crossing_menu: A tile's menu acts through the chat. Ask the agent about it puts the tile in the composer, named first, so the next Turn works there, the focus just after it; Ask the agent for one, on a free slot, names the tile it would go under, and where. Edit, export and a new tile open their widget at the conversation's foot, as home does already.
gallery_note_crossing_navigation: A navigation leaves an entry: each gesture on the canvas, a tile centered, a Branch opened, its Context shown, is named, and the conversation tells the last one on its thread, in your amber, merging the gestures before it until something else happens there. The agent reads it with your next Message.
gallery_note_crossing_drop: A tile carried off the canvas, under a mouse or a pen, is named where it is let go in the composer: the composer lights to take it, and the tile's name lands at the caret, the focus there. A finger never carries a tile: its way is the menu's Ask the agent about it, or @.
gallery_note_crossing_phone: On a phone the chat stays in front. A crossing brings the canvas forward to show what the chat pointed at, centered and glinting in your amber, then gives the chat back after a glance, the focus where it was. A hand on the canvas meanwhile keeps it in front, until the seam gives the chat back. A screen reader hears what was shown.
crossing_state_pointing: In the chat: hover or focus a tile named, or type @
crossing_state_turn: In the chat: run the Turn, then let a Key change a tile
crossing_state_canvas_seen: On the canvas: open a tile with a dot, and it goes
crossing_state_proposal: In the chat: point at a change, then accept or discard
crossing_state_drafting: In the chat: write a tile, pick its place
crossing_state_next_turn: In the chat: name a tile first, or don't, then send
crossing_state_canvas_center: On the canvas: center a tile, a double click or ⇧↵
crossing_state_menu_chat: In the chat: where the menu's agent lines land
crossing_state_canvas_menu: On the canvas: a right click, a long press or ⇧F10 on a tile or a free slot
crossing_state_navigation_chat: In the chat: the entries your gestures leave
crossing_state_canvas_navigation: On the canvas: center a tile, open a Branch, show its Context
crossing_state_drop_chat: In the chat: the composer, which takes a tile let go over it
crossing_state_canvas_drop: On the canvas: drag a tile out, onto the composer
crossing_state_phone: On a phone: tap a tile named, then wait, or take the canvas
crossing_menu_elsewhere: {said}: on home it opens in the chat, at the conversation's foot
gallery_state_hover_card_named: Above a line naming two tiles: the next stays within reach
deck_why_title: Intelligence has become common. Experience has not.
deck_why_1: Anyone can call on intelligence now, and so can every agent. What stays rare is experience: what a person comes to understand by caring about something, for a long time.
deck_why_2: You stand at the crossroads of the things you care about. Hexframe's bet is that this care deserves your best: to deepen what you understand of each of them, and to lay it out, what matters most first.
deck_why_3: Hexframe is where that understanding is built, and shared: with the world, and with the agents that work beside you.
deck_why_sun: In hexframe's universe, you are a sun. What you understand turns around you, and the agents work by its light.
deck_principles_intro: The look is futuristic because hexframe is a bet on a future worth wanting: space, imbalance, fine lines and light, not chrome. Six principles say how, and every piece of the screen answers to them.
deck_principles_light: Dark is the default, and light its equal: the same rules hold by day.
deck_chat_say_1: This is the chat. You and the agent talk here, and whatever a menu would do happens here too.
deck_chat_answer: Because the right words go further than any button. Ask as precisely as you need, and go as deep as you like.
deck_chat_say_2: Type / below to go to any slide, or write to me: your words take your voice.
deck_chat_page_title: The right words, and room to explore
deck_chat_page_intro: We believe in finding the right words, and a conversation is a good way to explore: it goes as precisely and as deep as you need, and nobody had to draw the menu first.
deck_chat_page_yours: Yours, in Newsreader, a light serif, behind an amber line
deck_chat_page_agents: The agent's, in Geist Mono, marked by a violet hex
deck_chat_page_agents_sample: I read Projects, then drafted Tooling under it.
deck_chat_page_interface: And the interface, in Geist, quietly
deck_chat_page_interface_sample: Everything else speaks low, so the two voices carry the page.
deck_chat_page_curve_text: The chat is cut along one curve, its only edge, and its scrollbar: a star rides it, lighting what you read. What the conversation asks of you comes as a zone, a fill and one fine line on top, running to the curve, never a box.
deck_chat_page_lacks_text: What a conversation brings in precision and depth, it can lack in clarity and simplicity: a whole system doesn't fit in a scroll of messages. That is the canvas's part.
deck_canvas_say_1: This is the canvas. Where the chat goes deep, the canvas stays clear: one tile, then the six it breaks into, what matters most first.
deck_canvas_say_2: Click the tile to open it. Click one of its six to open it in place, and double-click one to go in. The corner says where you are.
deck_tour_canvas_preview: A system as tiles: one tile, the six it breaks into, then theirs, what matters most first. Click this one to open it.
deck_tour_tile_preview: A title, a preview a reader decides by, at most 350 characters, and a body for the rest.
deck_tour_title_preview: What the tile is called, the first thing read.
deck_tour_preview_preview: What a reader needs to decide whether to open it.
deck_tour_body_preview: Everything else, in Markdown, read once it is open.
deck_tour_six_preview: A tile breaks into six at most, numbered round it from the north-west. Six forces a choice, and the choice is the point.
deck_tour_light_preview: A tile is drawn by its light, a fill lighter than the ground. Only the center keeps a line, a neutral one.
deck_tour_warm_preview: Amber belongs to you: the root of your own system holds the one warm light, and its glow stays with you as you move.
deck_tour_inside_preview: Inside a tile, its Context says what it is, beside what its children say it does. Its menu shows it: a right click, or a long press.
deck_tour_motion_preview: Children bloom out of their tile's heart and fold back into it. Going in centers a tile, alone and large, its preview whole.
deck_tour_why_six_preview: Six around one is about what a reader holds at a glance, and the ring closes on itself.
deck_tour_why_hexes_preview: A hexagon meets each of its six neighbours along a whole side: no corner left out, every neighbour equal.
deck_chapter_pick: Each piece shows on the canvas as I tell it here; pick another below.
deck_chapter_try: Pick one below: it runs on the whole screen, its end here and its end on the canvas.
deck_tokens_say_1: The tokens hold the look: every colour in the dark and in the light, the three fonts, the sizes, the motions. Amber is yours, violet the agent's, and nothing else is coloured.
deck_tokens_say_2: Every ink reads at 4.5:1 at least, on the ground and on a card, in both themes; switch the theme from the corner to see.
deck_answer: Nobody answers here yet: this is a presentation. Type / to go to a slide.
deck_composer_placeholder: Write, or type / to go to a slide
